questions.stem: The LARGEST organ of the human body is:
questions.explanation: Skin is the largest organ by surface area (~1.8 sq m) and by weight (~4 kg). Liver is the largest INTERNAL organ (~1.5 kg).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The LONGEST BONE in the human body is:
questions.explanation: Femur — about 48 cm in an adult, ~25% of body height. Smallest bone is the stapes (in the middle ear, 3 mm). Total adult bones: 206.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The pH of normal human BLOOD is:
questions.explanation: Blood pH is tightly regulated 7.35-7.45 by bicarbonate buffer + respiratory + renal mechanisms. Acidosis (<7.35) or alkalosis (>7.45) is medically dangerous. Gastric acid, by contrast, pH 1.5-3.5.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Match the ENDOCRINE GLAND with its hormone. A. Thyroid.  B. Pancreas.  C. Pituitary.  D. Adrenal medulla. List-II: 1. Thyroxine.  2. Insulin.  3. Growth hormone.  4. Adrenaline.
questions.explanation: Thyroid — thyroxine (T4) and T3, regulate metabolism. Pancreas (islets of Langerhans) — insulin (β-cells) + glucagon (α-cells). Pituitary ('master gland') — GH, prolactin, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH. Adrenal medulla — adrenaline (epinephrine).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Which VITAMIN is synthesised by the human skin in the presence of sunlight?
questions.explanation: UV-B light converts 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin to Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol). Deficiency → rickets in children, osteomalacia in adults. Food sources: fatty fish, egg yolk, fortified milk.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The FUNCTIONAL UNIT of the kidney is:
questions.explanation: Nephron — ~1 million per kidney. Structure: glomerulus (filtration) + Bowman's capsule + proximal tubule + loop of Henle + distal tubule + collecting duct. Neuron — nervous system. Alveolus — lung.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Consider the following about the HUMAN HEART. 1. It has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles. 2. The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the body via the aorta. 3. The right side pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs via the pulmonary artery. 4. The SA node is the natural pacemaker of the heart. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Pulmonary artery is the only artery carrying deoxygenated blood; pulmonary vein is the only vein carrying oxygenated blood. SA node in right atrium initiates electrical impulses (~72 beats per minute at rest).
